MA.thesis_one_line: Global card-payment duopolist with mid-teens revenue growth, 60% operating margin and low debt, but at 25.6x earnings and a 5.17% risk-free rate the price now needs about 11% a year of FCF growth for ten years, in line with the base case.
kill_criteria: Net revenue growth falls below 8% YoY (reported) for two consecutive quarters.
Adjusted operating margin compresses more than 300 bps YoY for two consecutive quarters.

Rules Relief Class settlement refused at the November 2026 final hearing, or amended beyond the June 2026 preliminary terms (10 bp interchange cut for 5 years, 1.25% standard-card rate for 8 years, merchants may decline some premium and commercial cards), with a written estimate of revenue effect above 1% of net revenue. (BVNK closed 3 Aug 2026, so the former 'fails to close' criterion is moot.)
A U.S. court ruling narrows or voids the Damages Class Settlement release (the April-2026 merchant suit), with an accrued or disclosed potential loss exceeding $1bn.
Consolidated net debt/TTM EBITDA exceeds 1.5x (from ~0.6x currently) without a corresponding buyback pause disclosed by management.
key_adverse_facts: New putative U.S. merchant class action (filed April 2026) is trying to void the scope of the 2023 Damages Class Settlement release, potentially reopening pre-2019 interchange claims at larger scale than the $296M currently reserved.
Portuguese consumer class action seeking ~$0.5bn (as of 2026-06-30) tied to the 2019 EU interchange resolution, unresolved.

Consolidated total debt is $24.6bn at 30 Jun 2026 (long-term $22,184m plus current $2,459m), up from $18.3bn long-term at YE2025, and BVNK ($1.5bn cash upfront, up to $300m contingent) closed 3 Aug 2026 after that balance sheet date.
U.S. MDL accrual fell from $637m to $149m through 2026 payments (10-Q); H1-26 operating cash flow ($6,772m) was below H1-25 ($6,983m) partly for that reason.

Rules Relief Class settlement received preliminary approval in June 2026 (final hearing November 2026; Walmart and others object, NACS signals appeal): 10 bp credit interchange cut for 5 years and merchant right to decline some premium cards, a mix risk for premium-card incentives.
data_conflicts: MA gives no formal numeric quarterly/annual guidance in its earnings releases, unlike triage's implicit framing of a specific forward growth number; this dossier relies on consensus (d4) and realized growth instead.
b1_live_scores.csv's ROE (289.7%) is a share-count/equity-base artefact of buybacks, not comparable across the sector; this dossier weights gross-profit/assets and OCF/assets instead.
FCF in d4 ($16.96bn) deducts only PP&E capex; including capitalised software ($727m TTM) and SBC ($615m TTM) equity FCF is $15,360m (RA5, 6 Oct 2026).
MA.confidence_in_thesis: medium-high: business quality and 8-quarter trend are strong, but after correcting the discount rate (5.17% risk-free, cost of equity about 9.7%) and FCF definition the market price is in line with, not below, the base case; litigation tail (April 2026 merchant suit) and rebate growth (+22% vs network revenue +10%) remain open.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row for MA. Corrected reverse DCF (RA5, 6 Oct 2026): equity FCF $15,360m (OCF $17,437m - PP&E $735m - software $727m - SBC $615m), market cap $499.5bn, cost of equity 9.7% (5.17% + beta 0.9 x ERP 5.0%), 10 years then terminal growth 4.0%: implied FCF growth about 11.5% a year (8.7% to 14.2% across r 9.0-10.5% and gT 3.5-4.5%) vs a base path of 13% fading to 8% (average 10.5%). The earlier 6.8% vs 13% used cost of equity 7.9% on a 4.2% risk-free rate and a 22x exit multiple.

MA.scenario_basis: Annualised from $567.65 (25 Sep 2026); NTM EPS $22.17 (price / 25.6x). Bear: EPS +7%/yr, exit P/E 19x, 0.7% dividend yield (about $516). Base: EPS +12%/yr, exit 23x, 0.6% yield (about $717). Bull: EPS +15%/yr, exit 27x, 0.5% yield (about $911). Exit multiples cut from 20/25/28x because the 10-year yield is 5.17%, not the 4.2% previously assumed.

MCO.thesis_one_line: Near-duopoly credit-rating agency plus a growing data/analytics arm, but the price already needs the beat-and-raise streak to continue.
kill_criteria: FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance is cut below the $16.50-$17.00 range reaffirmed/narrowed as of the 2026-07-22 release.
Consolidated revenue growth falls below the guided high-single-digit range (below 7% YoY) for two consecutive quarters.
MIS (ratings) transactional revenue declines YoY for two consecutive quarters.
Consolidated net debt/TTM EBITDA exceeds 3.0x (from ~1.35x currently).
Total Moody's shareholders' equity turns negative on the consolidated balance sheet (from $3,025M currently).
key_adverse_facts: Total Moody's shareholders' equity fell from $4,054M to $3,025M in six months (buybacks/dividends running ahead of retained earnings) - a thin cushion if a credit-cycle downturn coincided with a legal or refinancing shock.

2Q26 GAAP diluted EPS growth (+57% YoY) was inflated by a $181M one-time gain on business divestitures; adjusted EPS growth (+31% YoY) is the more representative figure and the GAAP headline should not be read as sustainable run-rate growth.
MIS transactional revenue (34% YoY growth in 2Q26) is a leveraged bet on global debt-issuance volumes and would fall quickly in a credit-market slowdown, with limited advance warning.
data_conflicts: b1_live_scores.csv's ROE (76.9%, cited by triage) is partly an artefact of the shrinking equity base described above, not pure operating economics; this dossier relies on operating cash flow and the guidance track record instead.
MCO.confidence_in_thesis: medium: guidance track record (4/4 releases raised or narrowed upward, with exact quoted numbers) is strong evidence of execution, but the reverse DCF shows the price already assumes that execution continues, leaving little margin of safety if the credit cycle turns.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for MCO in this run (not covered), so there is nothing to reconcile; the dossier's own reverse DCF (~11.7%/yr implied FCF growth) is close to the company's own guided/realized ~12-13%/yr trajectory, i.e. fairly priced rather than cheap.

MCO.scenario_basis: FCF/share $14.89 (TTM); NTM P/E 25.5x start; bear = 7%/yr EPS CAGR with exit P/E 20x and 1.0% avg dividend yield; base = 12%/yr EPS CAGR with exit P/E 25x (flat) and 0.9% yield; bull = 16%/yr EPS CAGR with exit P/E 28x and 0.8% yield; all over a 3-year horizon.

MRSH.thesis_one_line: World's largest insurance broker, priced cheaply on a reverse DCF, but a $2 billion Greensill lawsuit against two subsidiaries is still unresolved.
kill_criteria: The Credit Suisse Greensill claim (or any related Australian-proceedings claim) results in an incremental charge exceeding $500M in any single quarter, beyond the $425M already reserved.
GAAP diluted EPS declines YoY for a third consecutive quarter while adjusted diluted EPS growth also decelerates below 5% YoY.
Risk and Insurance Services segment underlying (organic) revenue growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters.
Consolidated net debt (excluding fiduciary funds)/TTM EBITDA exceeds 3.0x (from ~2.43x currently).
The quarterly dividend is cut or held flat for four consecutive quarters after the 2026-07-08 increase.
key_adverse_facts: The Company recorded a $425 million gross liability in Q1 2026 for the Greensill litigation (entity: Marsh Ltd. and Marsh Pty Ltd., subsidiaries); the Credit Suisse portion of the claim (~$2bn claimed) remains unresolved and management states additional charges are possible.

GAAP diluted EPS fell 5% YoY in H1 2026 ($4.99 vs $5.23) even though adjusted diluted EPS rose 8%; this is a real earnings-quality issue, not just a one-off optics problem, because the underlying liability is still developing.
Underlying (organic) revenue growth has decelerated over the last several quarters as commercial P&C insurance pricing has softened industry-wide.
An aviation/reinsurance information-sharing investigation and a long-running Brazil antitrust proceeding are both disclosed but under-specified in the filings reviewed (open items, not dismissed).
data_conflicts: d4_live_snapshot.parquet flags its own NTM P/E for MRSH as ntm_quality='caution' (15.3x); this dossier does not rely on that figure, using FCF-based multiples and a reverse DCF instead, consistent with the wave-3 lesson on not trusting an un-sanity-checked vendor NTM field.

Triage (Q05) cited 39% EPS growth and called 15.3x forward P/E fair; this dossier finds that figure is likely distorted by the Q1 2026 Greensill charge depressing the trailing EPS base used in a naive forward-growth calculation.
MRSH.confidence_in_thesis: medium: the underlying franchise quality and cheap reverse-DCF implied growth are well evidenced, but confidence is capped by the genuinely unresolved size of the Credit Suisse Greensill claim, which primary sources confirm could still grow.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for MRSH in this run (not covered), so there is nothing to reconcile; the dossier's own reverse DCF (~0.8%/yr implied FCF growth vs a base case of ~8%/yr) independently supports a 'cheap' view, tempered by the litigation reservation that keeps the verdict at INCLUDE-SMALL rather than INCLUDE.

MRSH.scenario_basis: FCF/share $10.03 (TTM); trailing P/E 20.9x start; bear = 3%/yr EPS CAGR (further Greensill charges) with exit P/E 16x and 2.3% avg dividend yield; base = 8%/yr EPS CAGR with exit P/E 19x and 2.2% yield; bull = 11%/yr EPS CAGR with exit P/E 21x and 2.0% yield; all over a 3-year horizon.
